prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate objective function for a GNN-based netlist tier-partitioner (2-tier 3D IC).
Hypothesis of the change: Replacing the saturating product-form cut probability with a fan-out-normalised star (pairwise) expansion sum over pins of (p_i - mean_p_net)^2 / (k-1) keeps a usable gradient on large/high-fan-out nets (clock, reset) so the partition actually decides those nets instead of leaving them saturated, reducing TNS via fewer badly-cut hub nets.
Rule-based digest (scores are improvement ratios vs. the official baseline; C1..C3 are the training circuits by size):
total=-0.867 robust(mean-std)=-0.440 min_case=-0.492 seed_std=0.125 tns_mean=-0.195 all_valid=True
  C1: score=-0.130 dWNS=-19.9% dTNS=-8.1% per-seed=[-0.16 -0.13 -0.10]
  C2: score=-0.246 dWNS=-22.7% dTNS=-21.4% per-seed=[-0.05 -0.18 -0.50]
  C3: score=-0.492 dWNS=-86.2% dTNS=-27.9% per-seed=[-0.33 -0.71 -0.44]
  partition stats vs baseline:
  C1: cut 137->171, wcut 421->540, crit_cross 0.011->0.033, repair_flips 103->112, changed-vs-baseline 24.2%
  C2: cut 318->351, wcut 1007->1148, crit_cross 0.000->0.055, repair_flips 238->238, changed-vs-baseline 16.8%
  C3: cut 582->637, wcut 1955->2196, crit_cross 0.069->0.296, repair_flips 353->347, changed-vs-baseline 19.1%
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID, first classify the failure (crash / non-finite loss / balance repair failure / timeout) and whether it is systematic or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which circuit/metric moved and the plausible mechanism (cut nets, critical-pair cross-tier, repair flips)? (3) is the seed spread acceptable? (4) one concrete next step. No preamble.

response: Hypothesis failed: all circuits worsened (total −0.867), with C3 worst (dWNS −86%, dTNS −28%). Cut nets, weighted cut, and critical-pair cross-tier crossings all rose (C3 crit_cross 0.069→0.296), and repair flips barely changed—so the fan-out-normalised star did not rescue hub nets; it increased crossings and criticality. Seed spread is high (std 0.125; C2 per-seed −0.05 to −0.50), indicating instability. Next step: gate the star term by fan-out (only apply above a threshold) or blend it with the product form, and re-test on C3 with more seeds.
